glossary_suggestions: Scope header says 1886–1890, but this sample is 1896–1902. Extend the clergy list with canonical forms for the priests who appear: Baltrukėnas/Bałtrukiewicz (pick one), Szołkowski, Tomaszewicz, Pujdak, Paszkanis, Butkiewicz, Lenkiewicz, Jarulaitis, Brzeziński. Without them every translator invents a variant (at least 7 spellings of Baltruken occur).
Add a rendering for "Мѣстнымъ" before a priest's rank. Use "vietinis kunigas vikaras" consistently; "vietos kunigas vikaras" also appears.

State explicitly that in "[X] kaime" / "[X] miestelyje" / "[X] vienkiemyje" the place name is a genitive (plural for -ai/-iai villages: Kovšanų kaime, not Kovšanai kaime). The current entry "[X] kaime" lets the nominative through in about 30 rows.

Lowercase "sakramento": "su visomis sakramento apeigomis". Capitalizing "Sakramento" copies Russian/Polish ecclesiastical capitalization of Таинства; standard Lithuanian writes common nouns in lowercase mid-sentence.

дѣвицею -> "mergina" reads as colloquial "girl" in a legal register and does not parallel "nevedęs" (холостымъ). Suggest "netekėjusi" (unmarried), the marital-status term used in Lithuanian civil and metrical translations, to pair with "nevedęs" and "našlė".

Maiden name: support the open question. "Onos, gim. Mockus" puts a masculine nominative surname after a woman's name and is not idiomatic. "Onos iš Mockų" matches "изъ Мокусовъ", was the actual usage in period Lithuanian church writing, and needs no invented feminine form.

Twins: the round-3 rule covers only both twins in one entry. Add the single-twin entry form "sūnus, vienas iš dvynių, gimęs" / "duktė, viena iš dvynių, gimusi" (and "viena iš trynukų"), because four different phrasings occur.
Add "того же Прихода" -> "tos pačios parapijos" and "Плунгянскаго Прихода" -> "Plungės parapijos". Both are in heavy use but absent from the glossary.

Women's surnames: clarify that a written -ская/-ская is rendered -ska (Jankovska, Račkovska), not the masculine -skis (Pranciška Jankovskis 0256, Marija Tomatevskis 0139, Ona Zavurskis 0233, Ona Meikovskis 0295) and not Russian -skaja (0096, 0259).
Wife formula: specify what to do when only the husband's surname (or only his given name) is written, e.g. "Domicelė, Stanimo [?] žmona", and the widow formula "Malvina, Donovskio našlė".
Standardize note markers: [sic], [taip parašyta], [kaip parašyta] and [taip juodraštyje] are all used. Pick one (e.g. [sic]) and use Lithuanian quotation marks „“ inside notes.
Godparents' estate: fix one order, e.g. "Krikštatėviai buvo valstiečiai A ir B". Both that and "Krikštatėviai, valstiečiai, buvo A ir B" appear.
Remove the duplicate list items (Игнацы and Агнешка are each listed twice).
overall: The skeleton formula is applied consistently: the date, the church, \"Krikštatėviai buvo\", the parents' template, \"gim.\" plus a nominative maiden name, and Petronėlė always with ė. The most common real error is grammatical: village names in the nominative plural before \"kaime\" (about 30 rows). Next come wildly inconsistent clergy name spellings, which the glossary requires to be uniform but does not list for this period. A handful of rows drop \"Sakramento\", write dates in words, or keep Russian suffixes (-ski, -skij, -ič, -skaja, -sk, -o) that the glossary forbids. A few genitive/nominative agreement slips occur in unmarried mothers' names and godparents' surnames. Not translation issues, but worth checking against the images: unmarked impossible or inverted dates in 0080_R1 (born 18 Jan, baptized 4 Jan), 0229_L4 (born 29 Jan, baptized 3 Jan), 0251_L1 (born 26 Jul, baptized 22 Jul), 0277_R1 (29 Feb 1902, not a leap year), 0182_R3 (\"1819\" with no [sic]) and 0054_L3 (born 2 May, baptized 25 May). 0109_L3 has an empty godparents field. Names were not flagged where they were plainly transliterated as read. The relayed user remark \"I think the ribbon is broken\" falls outside this review step and was not investigated; no files were written.
